[[2007]] [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] Player of the Year (Coaches) | awards = | records = }} '''Derrick JaVaughn Byars''' (born [[April 25]], [[1984]] in [[Memphis, Tennessee]]) is an [[United States|American]] [[basketball]] player who finished his [[college basketball|college]] career in 2007 at [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt University]]. He transferred to Vanderbilt in 2004 after playing for two years at the [[Virginia Cavaliers basketball|University of Virginia]]. ==High school career== Byars attended [[Ridgeway High School]] in Memphis, where he played for head coach [[Wesley Henning]] and won two [[Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Association]] (TSSAA) Class AA State Championships. As a sophomore (1999-2000), Byars was an honorable-mention all-State selection and led the Roadrunners to the Class AA State Championship. He averaged 16.4 points, 6.5 rebounds and 5.4 assists per game. As a junior, he again earned honorable mention All-State honors and was named Ridgeway's Most Valuable Player. He averaged 20.5 points, 7.2 rebounds and 5 assists. As a senior (2001-02), he averaged 23.2 points, 10 rebounds and 4.5 assists and led Ridgeway to its second TSSAA Class AA State Championship in three years. He was a fourth-team Parade All-America selection, the Gatorade Player of the Year in Tennesseee, the TSSAA Class AA Tournament Most Valuable Player and first-team All-State.{{cite web |url=http://virginiasports.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/byars_derrick00.html|title=Derrick Byars Profile (Virginia)|publisher=CSTV.com|accessdate=2007-03-08}} As impressive as he was on the court, Byars also excelled in the classroom, finishing high school with a 3.9 GPA.{{cite web |url=http://www.cavalierdaily.com/CVArticle.asp?ID=14063&pid=932|title=Derrick Byars Inside Out|publisher=CavalierDaily.com|accessdate=2007-03-08}} ==Collegiate career== ===Virginia=== Byars played for two seasons under then-Head Coach [[Pete Gillen]] at [[Virginia Cavaliers basketball|Virginia]]. He started 16 of Virginia's 31 games his freshman season (2002-03) and averaged 6.5 points per game. In his sophomore season (2003-04), he started 18 of Virginia's 31 games and averaged 7.5 points per game.{{cite web |url=http://vucommodores.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/byars_derrick00.html|title=Derrick Byars Profile (Vanderbilt)|publisher=CSTV.com|accessdate=2007-03-08}} After falling out with Gillen, Byars decided to transfer from Virginia. Vanderbilt, fresh off a run to the Sweet 16 of the [[2004 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]], was his first choice, but the Commodores had no scholarship positions available. Days before Byars was due to announce his transfer to [[University of Mississippi|Mississippi]], Vanderbilt reserve guard Adam Payton decided to transfer to [[College of William & Mary|William & Mary]], freeing up a scholarship for Byars.{{cite web |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2007/03/19/sports/ncaabasketball/19vandy.html|title=Commodores’ Success Is Built on Two Players Who Never Met|publisher=NYTimes.com|accessdate=2007-03-19}} He sat out the 2004-05 season as mandated by NCAA rules. ===Vanderbilt=== In his junior season (2005-06), Byars started all 30 games and finished second on the team in scoring at 12.4 points per game. He led the team with 3.2 assists per game. He was named SEC Player of the Week (Nov. 28-Dec. 4) after scoring 20 points on 7-of-8 shooting against [[Oregon Ducks|Oregon]] on November 30, 2005. A week later, he scored a season-high 25 points (including five 3-pointers) against [[Cincinnati Bearcats|Cincinnati]] on December 10, 2005.{{cite web |url=http://vucommodores.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/byars_derrick00.html|title=Derrick Byars Profile 2006-07|publisher=CSTV.com|accessdate=2007-03-08}} In his senior season (2006-07), Byars was named [[Southeastern Conference]] Player of the Year by the league's coaches, who also unanimously selected him to their All-SEC first team. He led Vanderbilt to a 22-12 record ([[Southeastern Conference|SEC East]]: 10-6, 2nd) and the Sweet 16 of the [[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]]. He led the Commodores in scoring with 17.0 points per game and was ranked among the SEC's top 10 in four other statistical categories. During SEC play, Byars averaged 19.1 points per game, second-best in the SEC. He scored 20 points or more eight different times, including a career-high 32 points against [[South Carolina Gamecocks|South Carolina]] on February 14, 2007. He followed that performance with 24 points in Vanderbilt's 83-70 victory over then-No. 1 [[Florida Gators|Florida]], which earned him SEC player of the week honors for the second time that season. {{cite web |url=http://www.tennessean.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20070308/SPORTS0602/703080416/1002|title=Coaches say Byars SEC's best|publisher=Tennessean.com |accessdate=2007-03-08}} Byars graduated from Vanderbilt on May 11, 2007 with a degree in sociology. In a mock-draft posted by InsideHoops.com, Byars was projected as the 18th pick in the first round of the NBA draft scheduled for June 28, 2007. {{cite web |url=http://www.tennessean.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=2007705090445|title=Byars may go late in first round|publisher=Tennessean.com|accessdate=2007-05-14}} ==Notes and references== {{reflist}} {{start box}} {{succession box|title=Coaches [[SEC Men's Basketball Player of the Year]]
